settings.heading: 13 years of teaching people to build
settings.story_text:
In 2012, James Marr returned from Canada with an unusual skill — the ability to build bicycle frames from bamboo. He opened a small workshop in London with a simple goal: prove that anyone could do it. No prior experience. No welding. Just bamboo, natural fibre, and your own two hands.

The first builders came for the craft. They stayed for the transformation. Engineers, artists, teachers, teenagers, retirees, prisoners — people who had never made anything with their hands came in and left differently. Quieter. More confident. Connected to something they'd made themselves.

What started as a weekend experiment became a movement. BBC frames have since been ridden 8,288 miles from Colombia to Tierra del Fuego, from London to New Zealand, across the Pamir Highway in winter, and on a daily Tokyo commute for over a decade. Over 4,000 people across 36 countries have built their own bamboo bicycle. Every one is unique. Every one is someone's favourite.
settings.founder_quote: If we want people to choose sustainable options, we need to offer something genuinely better than what polluting products can be.

settings.title: The Beginning
settings.description: Bamboo Bicycle Club founded in London by James Marr and Ian McMillan. James brought bamboo bicycle-building skills learned in Canada to share with others.

settings.title: First International Builders
settings.description: Builders from Germany, France, and the Netherlands travel to London. Kit demand grows from outside the UK.

settings.title: DIY Kits Launch
settings.description: After 2 years perfecting the process, home build kits launch — enabling people worldwide to build their own bamboo bikes. Featured in Huck Magazine and Inhabitat.

settings.title: Design Museum
settings.description: Featured in the Cycle Revolution exhibition at the Design Museum London. Live building demonstrations and world's first aerodynamic bamboo bicycle unveiled.

settings.title: World First
settings.description: Created world's first 3D printed bamboo bicycle in collaboration with Oxford Brookes University — pioneering new manufacturing techniques.

settings.title: Schools Programme Launches
settings.description: Southbank UTC runs the first structured school programme — 30 bikes built over two years, integrated into the Design & Technology curriculum.

settings.title: Kevin McCloud's Green Heroes
settings.description: Selected at Grand Designs Live for eco-friendly product design and sustainable manufacturing innovation — recognised alongside leading UK green brands.

settings.title: International Education — Kenya
settings.description: Munich workshop team teaches bamboo building in Kenya, transferring skills to local artisans. Knowledge-sharing model taken international.

settings.title: Social Enterprise
settings.description: Bamboo Mobility Project CIC registered — our social enterprise arm delivering OCN-accredited courses in sustainable manufacturing to prisons and schools.

settings.title: OCN Level 2 Accreditation
settings.description: OCN London Level 2 accreditation in Sustainable Manufacturing achieved — a nationally recognised qualification available to all programme participants.

settings.title: Kate Rawles Completes 8,288 Miles
settings.description: Environmental advocate Kate Rawles completes her Colombia → Tierra del Fuego expedition on 'Woody', her BBC-built bamboo bike. Zero frame failures.

settings.title: Toulouse Opens & Rwanda Partnership
settings.description: Toulouse workshop opens as BBC's third franchise location. Rwanda partnership launches with Urumuri — building local bamboo bicycle manufacturing capacity.

settings.title: Today
settings.description: 4,000+ people trained across 36+ countries. Investec Beyond Business winner. Financial Times feature. James Timpson government endorsement. And we're just getting started.

settings.heading: What Our Builders Say
settings.subheading: From London workshops to Tokyo commutes to prison rehabilitation programmes

settings.title: Sustainability
settings.text: Bamboo regrows from the same root system in 3–5 years — a rapidly renewable grass we can work by hand. And because our builders make their own frames, they learn to maintain and repair them too, so they last.

settings.title: Craftsmanship
settings.text: We teach traditional handcraft skills in a modern context — reconnecting people with the act of making something real, that lasts for years, with their own two hands.

settings.title: Community
settings.text: From London workshops to prisons, schools, and corporate events — we build more than bikes. We build confidence, skills, and the kind of pride that only comes from making something yourself.

settings.name: James Marr
settings.bio: James learned bamboo bicycle building in Canada before returning to London to share the knowledge. He founded BBC in 2012 with Ian McMillan and has since built programmes recognised by the Financial Times, the UK Prisons Minister, Investec, and Kevin McCloud. He leads BBC's mission to make sustainable craftsmanship accessible to everyone.

settings.name: Toulouse Workshop
settings.bio: BBC's French home, opened May 2024, bringing bamboo bike building to the heart of cycling country. Workshops run in French and English. France is BBC's highest-converting international market.

settings.name: Amersfoort Workshop
settings.bio: Our Dutch workshop serving the Netherlands and surrounding regions. Home to a thriving community of European bamboo bike builders.
